resumed_from: No earlier fix attempt (no fix commit, no uncommitted edit in this role's paths at start). This step pushed a work-in-progress commit d6675b1; two orchestrator snapshots (fafbd02, d2dd41b) then picked up some later edits while it ran; the fix commit carries the rest.
summary: BFL-R1..R10: all 10 fixed (R9 by wording in SPEC and the code; the web's PAST_RULE_NOTE string is handed to the integration). The loop now spends one budget a cycle for the prefetch and the append step's NWS and NWPS requests; due refreshes are warmed at a pace that leaves NWPS room and run outside the job workers; a refresh can no longer make a bundle worse; satellite pass keys tried survive a restart; product texts refused by Fire-3d's own limit are asked again. Year lists use each product's own time and the newest product's end, leave out floods still in effect, follow registry aliases and live VTEC keys, and name the issuing office. Past floods answer 409 PAST_NO_BUNDLE to Prepare and never answer today's model output.

findings.title: Refresh rebuilds removed member gauges, impacts, credits and NWM series (NWPS limit used up by the cycle)
findings.verified: Yes, in the code paths named: the cycle's prefetch (up to 20 series) and append reads (12 gauges x 2) were outside any shared budget; refresh jobs were submitted straight into the job workers in the same limiter window; merge_rebuilt_gauges kept the rebuilt gauge's fields ({**fresh}), dropped members missing from the rebuild and returned an unavailable rebuild unchanged (so a failed rebuild overwrote a good gauges.json); nothing put back lost nwm_series files or layers. A test with NWPS answering SourceBusy during a refresh reproduced the loss (members, impacts, reach, series).
findings.fix: floods/live.py: (1) one budget a cycle: PREFETCH_MAX (20) covers the prefetch (at most 20 - APPEND_SHARE 8 = 12; caps hvtec 6, zones 3, series 3) and the append step's requests (alerts_cost for the products' NWS requests, exact _gauge_cost for NWPS gauge reads, at most GAUGE_READS_MAX). (2) Due refreshes go to STATE.pending; the loop's own runner (run_refreshes, task fire3d-flood-refreshes) warms each flood's NWPS gauge details, series and NWM reach series into the HTTP cache while more than NWPS_RESERVE (10) of NWPS's 30 slots a minute are free (warm_nwps, at most WARM_MAX_S 240 s), then submits the refresh job; the first-cycle auto-build warms the same way; no job worker waits. (3) refresh_job_fn snapshots the earlier files and runs keep_what_the_rebuild_lost after the rebuild: product versions merged (an unavailable rebuild keeps the earlier answer and layer_status); merge_rebuilt_gauges(older, rebuilt, members) -> (merged, kept): unavailable rebuild keeps the earlier gauges.json, a member read only from the gauge map keeps its earlier NWPS detail with the newer reading (keep_detail), a current member left out is put back, a gauge that left the flood stays as a nearby gauge with its history, GAUGE_DETAIL_DOWN dropped when no member is left without detail, credits re-added; earlier nwm_series files of members put back; naip, water_forecast, floodplain, water_model and water_satellite (outage only, never over NASA's no_image) that were ok keep their earlier files, layer entry, layer_status (own time) and credit; the manifest gains REFRESH_KEPT. (5) check_bundle --hazard flood notes member gauges of the summary missing from gauges.json, members with the map's reading only, and REFRESH_KEPT warnings.

findings.title: A Flash Flood Warning still in effect showed as a past flood under an alias id
findings.verified: Yes: the cached 2026 list (built 06:22 UTC) had 6 rows whose events ended after the build, among them Chatsworth (KFFC.FF.W.0081/0082) under flood-20261105-blue-ridge-flash-flood-2c43eb; the alias line blue-ridge -> toccoa was written after the build (reg.id_for already follows aliases at build time, so the stale disk copy, not assign, kept the old id); _with_live_rows matched by id only.
findings.fix: history.build_rows(..., now=): a group whose newest product had not expired at build time is left out (the live list serves it); history.canonical_rows maps served year rows through the registry's aliases at request time (rows landing on one id merged, aliases updated), used by year_list and cached_rows (so find). api/floods._with_live_rows (every year) serves a year row as the live row holding its id or any of its VTEC keys, each once. _resolve gains a year-alias step (an old id of a year row -> the canonical year row, resolved_from 'alias'); an old id of a live flood goes to catalog's alias step.
tests: test_floods_history.py::test_a_year_row_whose_warning_is_live_is_served_as_the_live_flood (a still-active VTEC key held by a live flood under another id)

findings.title: 'Prepare 3D data' for a listed past flood answered 'This flood is not listed. (HTTP 404)'
findings.verified: Yes: start_flood_build called build.gate, which uses catalog.resolve (no year step).
findings.fix: start_flood_build resolves with _resolve; a year-list flood answers 409 with history.PAST_NO_BUNDLE ('Fire-3d prepares 3D data for current floods only: NWS's forecast maps, the model and river forecasts are not kept for a past flood's dates.'); the web shows a 409's detail verbatim. cli build-flood refuses a past flood with the same text (exit 1). An at_ms-aware build is not attempted (build.py is not this role's file, and today's maps are wrong for a past flood).
findings.real_data: POST /api/floods/flood-20250403-rough-river-flood-781c6b/build -> 409 PAST_NO_BUNDLE; cli build-flood -> refused, exit 1. Screenshot brief5-backend-flood-live-fix-past-rough-forensic.png: after the Prepare click the card shows PAST_NO_BUNDLE, not 'not listed'.

findings.title: Every restart queued full rebuilds (satellite passes tried lived only in memory)
findings.verified: Yes: STATE.seen_passes was in memory only, and with no measured image (acq None) every listed pass counted as new.
findings.fix: Pass keys tried are kept in data/floods/live_state.json ({seen_passes: {fid: {built_ms, keys}}}, at most 60 keys a flood, floods with a bundle only). new_passes: with a measured image, passes newer than it and not tried; without one, the passes listed at the first check after a build (sensed before it ran) are taken as the ones the build saw, so only passes that appear later count.
findings.real_data: Restart on a fresh copy of the same bundles plus live_state.json: no 'satellite' refresh queued again (the first run had St. Johns and Moenkopi 'satellite'); only 'rfc_fim' (NWS's forecast maps had new times).

findings.title: The append step's NWS requests (zones, product texts) were outside PREFETCH_MAX
findings.verified: Yes: append_bundle called zones.flood_alerts (up to 20 zone outlines and 6 product texts on NWS_LIMITER) for up to 8 bundles with no budget.
findings.fix: alerts_cost(summary) (caches only): the national answer when its 2-min copy expired, uncached zone outlines up to ZONE_FETCH_MAX, uncached product texts up to HVTEC_FETCH_MAX (exact _hvtec_cost). append_bundle fetches the products' answer only when that fits the cycle's budget; else the products wait for a later cycle (the prefetch warms their zones and texts); gauges are still appended.

findings.title: A product refused by Fire-3d's own limiter was marked tried and never retried
findings.verified: Yes: hvtec() added the id to hvtec_tried before calling nws.product_hvtec.
findings.fix: The id is added only after NWS answered or failed (SourceError), never on SourceBusy.

findings.title: PAST_RULE counts forecast or observed H-VTEC severity; the wording said 'reached'
findings.verified: Yes: H-VTEC's severity field is the forecast or observed flood severity; IEM's CSV does not say which (no crest time), so observed-only cannot be selected from the bulk route.
findings.outcome: fixed (backend wording); web string handed to the integration
findings.fix: SPEC 8.10 and history.py now say 'reached or were forecast to reach moderate or major flood stage' (max_category likewise forecast or observed, as for live floods). PAST_RULE_NOTE lives in web/src/ui/shell/floodCopy.ts (not this role's file): the as-built note asks the integration to change it to the same wording.
